trajectory_summary: This call opens with a highly cooperative, self-motivated customer and never loses that footing — the shape is mostly energy-built with a mid-call efficiency dip during bill-photo collection. The rep completes verify, qualifies credit and utility, collects a usable bill image, and lands a booked Monday 10AM appointment, though several coaching-relevant misses (workshop system probe, roof-replacement cross-sell, time-constraint hedge, thin button-up) sit underneath a clean surface outcome.

observed_outcome.quote: Yeah. Sounds good. I'll go ahead and get you done for Monday at ten
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Monday) and time (10AM) were agreed and confirmed as a phone appointment; the wife was identified as co-title-holder at 02:32 but never explicitly invited or confirmed for the Monday call, so co_owner_confirmed is false despite booking.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked for a dollar bill amount ('do you know how much you're paying on average?'). The call instead went straight from utility confirmation to requesting the kWh usage document itself, so there is no dollar figure captured or available to flip.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: So, yeah, we just need to look at the last twelve months of kilowatt hours. You should be able to find that on your recent electric bill.
bill_document_audit.result_quote: Perfect. Yeah. That's, that's the one. Yep. It's got the, the one month there and the chart.
bill_document_audit.reasoning: Rep explicitly requested the utility bill's kWh data and offered text/email; the customer sent bill photos via text during the call, and after two false starts the rep confirmed receipt of the correct chart at 11:51.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: I've always had an interest in solar, and, we've talked about converting our house. I have a, a workshop that I currently have a small solar system in.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The customer gave a rich, specific reason (long-standing interest, existing workshop system, household conversation) but the rep responded only with 'Okay. Awesome. Sounds good. Perfect.' and never referenced this motivation again, including in the closing recap or the appointment framing.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Front-load bill instructions to cut collection time
primary_coaching_focus.quote: We do need to see at least one specific number for one month.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep burned roughly 6-7 minutes (05:00 to 11:51) across three photo attempts because the initial ask never specified what number/graph to look for. A precise upfront instruction ('look for the bar chart of monthly kWh — read me the total for any single month') would collapse this to under two minutes and is a repeatable, coachable fix.

key_moments.quote: I currently have a small solar system in [the workshop].
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses an existing small solar system on a separate structure (the workshop) while explaining their interest — this is a depth signal the interest_in_solar item calls for expanding on, but the rep moves straight to 'Okay. Awesome. Sounds good. Perfect.' without asking who installed it, how it's performing, or how long they've had it.

key_moments.quote: I don't want to, I know at some point I'm gonna have to replace the roof on my house, but, I wanna keep keep it clean right now.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer explicitly flags a future planned roof replacement on the house — a textbook cross-sell trigger for Ion's in-house roofing team — and the rep responds only with 'Sure. Yeah. Not a problem,' filing it rather than bridging.

key_moments.quote: Someone else did it. Yeah. Definitely, don't blame me there. Awesome.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer reveals they explored DIY solar and wanted cost ideas — a prior_designs signal and a live curiosity hook about what a DIY approach would have cost versus Ion's design. The rep laughs it off and moves straight into bill collection without exploring what the customer found or what cost expectations they're carrying in.

key_moments.quote: About how long does it take?
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a direct time-constraint protocol trigger. The correct pattern is a firm anchor ('it's a 30-minute call'), but the rep hedges: 'really just depends on, how many questions you have.' That vagueness is exactly what the schema warns increases no-show risk.
